newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv says acquisition beats strong crown.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv says acquisition beats strong crown.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment manufacturer Autoliv said on Thursday the negative effect of a stronger crown on its 1996 earnings was outweighed by a positive effect from an acquisition.
Posting a 13 percent rise in 1996 after financial items profits to 1.15 billion crowns, Autoliv said its sales in the year to December 31 rose 14 percent to 11.6 billion crowns.
A noted improvement in sales was reported in the fourth quarter when sales rose 26 percent from a year earlier -- 27 percent for airbags and 26 percent for seat belts.
However Autoliv said prices continued to fall throughout the year.
Autoliv said sales of airbags rose by 13 percent to 5.5 billion crowns during the year.
New customers, including Audi and Volkswagen which ordered side airbags, contributed to the rise.
The sale of seat belts rose by 15 percent to 6.1 billion crowns.

Autoliv said the increase in sales outperformed growth in the most important underlying market -- the manufacture of light vehicles in Europe -- which rose an estimated three percent in the same period.
Autoliv late last year announced a proposal to merge with the automotive safety production operations of U.S. group Morton International Inc to form a multi-billion dollar airbag operation.
The company said a prospectus for the merger will be sent to shareholders in March.
Autoliv proposed a dividend of 2.75 crowns a share which is a 22 percent rise from last year's dividend of 2.25 crowns.
